geometry_edits.rationale: Introduce a ground spine so the split-wing/courtyard logic anchors to the active access edge instead of floating as a purely sectional gesture.
Keep the connector active so the void remains a public threshold rather than a detached cut.
Open the split a bit more to strengthen the courtyard/public void figure and reduce the sealed-box effect.

graph_edits.rationale: Align the courtyard opening to the program-frame west side, which corresponds to the verified access edge, so the public void becomes a legible street threshold rather than an internal subtraction.
Increase the courtyard carve so the void reads as a meaningful public open space with clearer ground consequence.
Lower the bridge/terrace link slightly to strengthen the occupied threshold condition and make the connector read as part of the active ground/public section.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early massing idea in three and four views: one primary low block, one vertical/raised central element, and a carved-through court/slot. It responds somewhat to the parcel and the thick blue frontage by keeping a perimeter mass with a visible ground response, but the access-edge articulation is not strongly resolved; the public void is present yet feels more like an internal subtraction than a clearly aligned street threshold. The silhouette is only moderately convincing because the central rise is abrupt and slightly stair-like, but not fatally fragmented. Program-wise, the mass can plausibly support neighborhood living, yet it is still hovering between a courtyard-terrace building and a more generic bridged object; the section does not yet fully prove the active ground edge plus calm upper hierarchy contract. It therefore fails hard pass on program fit, though it is not an outright typology mismatch.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is culturally oriented and more sculptural, but the void-and-connector logic is transferable to neighborhood living.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a clear central void and a legible bridge/connector above the ground threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More campus/office-like than the candidate, but the spatial hierarchy and courtyard organization are relevant.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking wings around a courtyard with elevated links and calm upper massing.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Single-story retail/hospitality is scale-light relative to the candidate; useful mainly for frontage and entry logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple street-facing pavilion massing with a small entry setback/canopy and clear ground response.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a much larger housing typology and the candidate should not copy the long-span hillside profile or resort-like scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/stepped residential massing can support neighborhood living when the terraces are tied to usable open space.

warnings: Visible massing is coherent but only moderately aligned to the verified access edge; the street/public threshold should be more explicit.
The upper raised element risks reading as a sculptural plug unless tied more clearly to the courtyard/terrace section logic.
The silhouette is close to a stepped/bridged object, but the section still needs stronger program consequence to avoid generic object-building reading.
